```{r}
#| label: setup
library(tidyverse)
library(plotly)
library(DT)
library(janitor)
```


```{r}
#| title: "Why London? (UK Regions Overview 2023)"
uk_data <- read_csv("business_survival.csv") %>%
  clean_names() %>%
  drop_na(area) %>%
  filter(str_detect(code, "^E12")) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = starts_with("x"), 
    names_to = "year", 
    values_to = "business_count"
  ) %>%
  mutate(year = as.numeric(str_replace(year, "x", "")))

p_uk <- uk_data %>%
  filter(year == 2023) %>%
  arrange(desc(business_count)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = reorder(area, business_count), y = business_count, fill = area)) +
  geom_col() +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(x = "Region", 
       y = "Total Businesses") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "none")

ggplotly(p_uk)
```

```{r}
# 1. Read data and clean names
raw_data <- read_csv("business_survival.csv") %>%
  clean_names() %>%
  drop_na(area) %>%
  filter(str_detect(code, "^E09"))
```

```{r}
# 2. Reshape from wide to long format
long_data <- raw_data %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = starts_with("x"), 
    names_to = "year", 
    values_to = "business_count"
  ) %>%
  mutate(year = as.numeric(str_replace(year, "x", "")))
```


## Row {height=25%}
```{r}
#| content: valuebox
#| title: "Total Areas Tracked"
#| icon: map
#| color: primary
list(value = length(unique(long_data$area)))
```

```{r}
#| content: valuebox
#| title: "Years Covered"
#| icon: calendar3
#| color: success
list(value = paste0(min(long_data$year), " - ", max(long_data$year)))
```

```{r}
#| content: valuebox
#| title: "Max Businesses in a Region (2023)"
#| icon: building
#| color: warning
max_biz_2023 <- long_data %>% filter(year == 2023) %>% summarize(max(business_count)) %>% pull()
list(value = max_biz_2023)
```


## Row {height=75%}
```{r}
#| title: "Business Trend over 20 Years (Top 5 Areas)"
# Get top 5 areas in 2023
top_5_areas <- long_data %>%
  filter(year == 2023) %>%
  arrange(desc(business_count)) %>%
  slice(1:5) %>%
  pull(area)

p1 <- long_data %>%
  filter(area %in% top_5_areas) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = year, y = business_count, color = area)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point(size = 2) +
  labs(x = "Year", 
       y = "Number of Businesses",
       color = "Area") +
  theme_minimal()

ggplotly(p1)
```

```{r}
#| title: "Top 10 Areas by Business Count in 2023"
p2 <- long_data %>%
  filter(year == 2023) %>%
  arrange(desc(business_count)) %>%
  slice(1:10) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = reorder(area, business_count), y = business_count, fill = area)) +
  geom_col() +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(x = "Area", 
       y = "Total Businesses") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "none")

ggplotly(p2)
```
